invention.ref: An Egyptian bone comb in Cambridge is dated to ca. 4000–3500 BCE; the timeline uses the start of this range as an early surviving example
invention.ref_zh: 剑桥馆藏埃及骨梳约为公元前4000—3500年；时间轴取区间起点，表示早期实物见证

locations.place_label_en: Egypt (Predynastic bone comb; precise findspot unrecorded)

notes: 梳子没有已确认的单一发明者。本条以前4000—3500年的埃及骨梳作为可核实的早期实物见证，并不宣称它是世界上最早的梳子。时间轴采用该区间起点，地图按馆藏记录只定位到埃及。前3200—3100年的埃及象牙梳还显示了装饰和仪式用途。
notes_en: No single inventor is established. The Egyptian bone comb dated to 4000–3500 BCE is a verifiable early surviving example, not a claim to the world’s first comb. The timeline uses the range’s beginning and the map locates only the documented country. A later Egyptian ivory comb dated to 3200–3100 BCE also shows decorative and ceremonial functions.
summary_zh: 梳子用排列的齿整理头发。埃及留下约公元前4000—3500年的骨梳，后来的象牙梳还刻有动物图案，兼具装饰和仪式用途。现存实物不足以确定梳子的唯一发源地。
summary_en: Combs arrange hair with rows of teeth. Egyptian bone examples date to 4000–3500 BCE; later carved ivory combs also had decorative and ceremonial roles. A single birthplace remains unproven.
